feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads well overall, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with increasing scope, budget/governance ownership, and strong digital transformation credibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete detail (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack), which strengthens impact.  
- Strong alignment between headline, summary, competencies, and experience; the profile is coherent and targeted.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Fix writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation is inconsistent in lists (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs no Oxford comma elsewhere); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” instead. No obvious misspellings, but tightening repetition of “workflow(s), systems, and coordination” would improve readability.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive value proposition and fewer phrases repeated elsewhere in skills and experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct punctuation.
- Lead with seniority and sector relevance: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience supporting mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations.”
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter summary of outcomes: cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, governance, and audience-focused content systems.
- Add one differentiator reflected in recent roles, such as Drupal/web platform transformation, analytics infrastructure, or AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” are already echoed in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The current intro overlaps heavily with work experience language; keep it high-level and brand-focused rather than listing channels.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills sections. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, leadership-level phrasing and remove lower-level items like “Web & CMS administration,” which are better covered in Technical + IT.
- Standardize wording for parallel structure, e.g., “Digital strategy and transformation,” “Editorial workflow and governance,” “Analytics and performance reporting.”
- Prioritize the most market-relevant strengths: digital strategy, platform modernization, editorial systems, cross-channel communications, analytics, and stakeholder leadership.
- Possible rewrite: Digital strategy and transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Platform modernization and CMS governance • Editorial workflow and content operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance insights • Systems and process design • Stakeholder and cross-functional leadership • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” duplicate Topline Skills/Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, leadership, and the most distinctive recent contributions, especially AI search and Drupal-based campaign/platform work.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact and client scope: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 sharper points; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics + governance/usability into one operations-focused bullet.
- Rewrite for action + result: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits that improved publishing flexibility and campaign delivery.” Add metrics if available: launch speed, traffic, engagement, publisher adoption, reduced support time.
- Elevate the strongest differentiator: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” overlaps heavily with the NACo Director role; keep this item focused on new consulting impact and current initiatives.
- Microsite and AI-search details also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team/operational scope, and what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a tighter summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: email performance, social growth/engagement, reporting adoption, production cost/time savings from the in-house studio, or governance efficiency gains.
- Tighten phrasing and parallel structure: start each bullet with a strong verb (Led, Built, Expanded, Standardized) and avoid broad terms like “strengthened” unless paired with a result.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” and recurring video/programming overlap with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- The video studio bullet may overlap with Recent Projects/older NACo entries unless framed as a leadership-scale capability build.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to the operational scale-up phase and emphasize outcomes, not general support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing during a period of organizational growth.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable impact where possible: newsletter growth, open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct action: “Standardized digital publishing workflows and editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the footer project and the 2015–2018 role; keep it only if you add distinct scale/results.
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved workflows” risk repeating the Director role’s governance language; frame this as implementation/operations, not enterprise leadership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent role bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership themes and avoid repeating generic phrasing already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive terms:
- Enterprise digital leadership
- Content governance and editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications strategy
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” to “cross-channel communications strategy” for concision and to avoid repeating “leadership” from the header.
- “Editorial systems and governance” is good, but “content governance and editorial operations” better reflects the operational scope shown in recent roles.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise content governance for high-volume publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “audience-focused content planning” are already implied in the header summary.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies (“Advocacy and public-sector communications”); use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work: Drupal-led modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented list: Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Move lower-priority or less central platforms from this topline item: consider dropping WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages unless they are important for the target role.
- Use “Front-end implementation” instead of listing languages first; it reads more senior and execution-focused.
- If space allows, add one outcome cue: “Drupal modernization for large public-facing sites” to echo recent 10,000+ page migration work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills selective, not exhaustive.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating too many generic phrases verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” To earn its place as a topline skill block, it should emphasize decision-making and business impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording and group related items: “Dashboarding & leadership reporting” instead of separate reporting terms.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so this section should stay sharper and more execution-focused.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and tied to recent leadership-level delivery rather than listing production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from task list to capability list: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event and advocacy content production”
- Emphasize scope/seniority over hands-on basics; “studio operations” alone feels junior—“in-house studio buildout and operations” better reflects the Director role.
- If space allows, add one outcome cue: “supporting advocacy programming and recurring multimedia content” to connect skills to business use.
- Keep terminology consistent with the CV: use “livestream and hybrid event delivery” rather than mixing “livestreaming” and “virtual event production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This partially duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; consider trimming one version.
- “Video production and editing” overlaps with older experience bullets, so avoid over-weighting editing unless it remains a current strength.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeat the same tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show proficiency level or primary use: “Drupal (enterprise content platforms, migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Put the most relevant/recent platform first and consider dropping weaker/older tools if space is tight; Drupal is clearly the anchor.
- If accurate, add version/scope for credibility: “Drupal 9/10” or “SharePoint Online.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS Platforms” for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the CV unless it supports a specific portfolio or deployment story elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add level/scope cues: Front-end development for Drupal-based sites, API integrations, tag management, edge scripting, and deployment automation
- Consider replacing older/basic terms with stronger specifics where possible: e.g., custom Drupal theming, CI/CD workflows, serverless scripting, analytics/tag deployment

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or make this one more implementation-focused.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap with analytics tooling; decide whether it belongs here or under Data/Analytics.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider replacing 1–2 names with a brief qualifier elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate,” since impact matters more than breadth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack” and “Teams” are common workplace tools; unless used administratively or for workflow orchestration, they add little differentiation.
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/operational context shown in recent roles. Make it tighter and more strategic by emphasizing enterprise email/member engagement platforms over listing brands only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with scope wording: Enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations and member engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- Put Dynamics 365 first, since it reads as the most enterprise/recent platform; keep Mailchimp last as the lightest-weight tool

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about newsletters/email; avoid adding generic phrases like “email campaigns” unless you add a distinct capability such as segmentation, journeys, or member communications
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider naming it in the NACo experience instead of expanding this skills line further

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup role rather than showing concrete contributions. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and content production, with any available scale metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and outcomes: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Split the rest into 2 concise impact points: one on the website refresh, one on multimedia/program delivery and informal supervision.
- Add measurable detail if possible: size of site refresh, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Possible phrasing: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format if accurate.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” risks repeating later operations-focused entries; keep this lighter and more foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation/program support plus that first-launch achievement.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia materials to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Keep it to 1–2 lines; this is an older role, so prioritize the podcast launch and cross-functional coordination over general responsibilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production and multimedia materials,” which overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Don’t overemphasize video/media leadership here; later NACo roles show that progression more strongly.
